s:
Arrange the following Acts of India in chronological order as per the year in which they were enacted.

s:
With reference to India, consider the following Central Acts:
1. Import and Export (Control) Act, 1947
2. Mining and Mineral Development (Regulation) Act, 1957 Environmental Legislation PMF IAS E&E – 83
3. Customs Act, 1962

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: Which of the following statements correctly explains the purpose of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 in India?
o: It was enacted to promote industrial growth without any environmental restrictions.
It focuses only on the protection of wildlife species and national parks.
It provides a framework for protecting and improving the environment and controlling all forms of pollution.
It was introduced to regulate forest revenue and timber trade.
x: The EPA 1986 is an umbrella law giving a framework to protect and improve the environment and control all forms of pollution; it is not about industrial growth, only wildlife, or timber revenue.

s:
What is true about Sunderban Wetland?

A. Sundarbans in West Bengal and other ecologically sensitive areas identified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 shall be treated as Critical Vulnerable Coastal Areas (CVCA).

B. These regions will be managed with the involvement of coastal communities, including fisher folk who depend on coastal resources for their sustainable livelihood.
o: Both A and B are true
Neither A nor B is true
x: Under the CRZ Notification 2011 (issued under the EPA), the Sundarbans and other identified ecologically sensitive areas are Critical Vulnerable Coastal Areas, managed with coastal communities including fisherfolk – both true.

s: After which environmental disaster did the Environment Protection Act, 1986 come into existence?
x: The EPA 1986 followed the Bhopal gas tragedy of December 1984; Ennore, the vulture crisis and Pasarlapudi are unrelated.

s:
Consider the following statements:
The Environment Protection Act, 1986 empowers the Government of India to

A. state the requirement of public participation in the process of environmental protection, and the procedure and manner in which it is sought

B. lay down the standards for emission or discharge of environmental pollutants from various sources
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The EPA empowers the Centre to lay down emission and discharge standards, but says nothing about public participation, so 2 only (UPSC 2019).

s: Which one of the following has been constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, of 1986?

s: Which one of the following has been constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
x: The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted under Section 3(3) of the EPA 1986 to regulate groundwater development.

s:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal (NGT):

A. The NGT shall consist of not less than five but subject to maximum of 10 full time judicial members.

B. To be appointed as the Chairperson of the Tribunal, a person must be a judge of the Supreme Court or the High Court.
x: The NGT Act provides for not less than 10 and up to 20 full-time judicial members (and as many expert members), not 5 to 10. src: APPSC Asst. B.C Welfare Officers, Royalty Inspector in A.P.
s: Which organization in India has been set up for the purpose of effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources?
x: The National Green Tribunal (NGT Act 2010) was set up for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources. The National Environment Tribunal of 1995 never came into force.

s: National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established to
o: Handle cases related to environmental protection and pollution control
x: The NGT exists to decide cases on environmental protection and pollution control quickly. Monitoring pollution and setting emission or water-quality standards are regulator (CPCB/SPCB) jobs, not the tribunal's.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal ?

I. It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.

II. NGT is bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

III. NGT has six places of sitting throughout the country.
x: I is correct (NGT Act 2010). II is wrong: the NGT is not bound by the CPC 1908 and follows natural justice. III is wrong: the NGT sits at five places (Principal Bench New Delhi and zonal benches at Pune, Bhopal, Chennai and Kolkata), not six.

s: National Green Tribunal’s (NGT) headquarters is situated at :
x: The NGT's principal bench and headquarters are in New Delhi; Kolkata and Chennai host zonal benches, and Mumbai has none (the western bench is at Pune).

s: What is the full form of NGT?
x: NGT stands for National Green Tribunal, set up under the NGT Act 2010.

s: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) came into force in:
x: The NGT was established and the NGT Act brought into force on 18 October 2010, so 'October 2010' is correct.

s: National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established by the Government of India in:
x: The NGT was established in 2010 (18 October 2010) under the NGT Act 2010.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
s: The Supreme Court has asked which state government to deposit Rs.100 crore fine imposed by NGT?
x: On 3 July 2019 the Supreme Court told Meghalaya to deposit the Rs 100 crore the NGT had imposed (4 Jan 2019) for failing to curb illegal coal (rat-hole) mining; it allowed the money to be moved from the state's Environment Protection and Restoration Fund to the CPCB, for restoration only.

s: Who organized the World Environment Conference at New Delhi in March, 2017?
x: The World Conference on Environment in New Delhi (25-26 March 2017, inaugurated by President Pranab Mukherjee) was organised by the National Green Tribunal.

s:
How is the National Green Tribunal (NGT) different from Central Pollution Control Board (CDCB)

I. The NGT has been established by an ACt, whereas the CPCB has been created by an executive order of the Government.

II. The NGT provides environmental Justice and helps reduce the burden of litigation in the higher courts whereas CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells, and aims to improve the quality of air in the country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement I is wrong: the CPCB is a statutory body constituted under the Water Act 1974, not by an executive order. Statement II is right: the NGT gives environmental justice and reduces litigation in higher courts, while the CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells and improves air quality.

s: Which government body has recently (January 2022) constituted a ‘Fly Ash Management and Utilization Mission’ with the objective of coordinating and monitoring the issues related to handling and disposal of fly ash and other associated issues?
x: In January 2022 the NGT constituted the Fly Ash Management and Utilization Mission to coordinate and monitor the handling, disposal and use of fly ash from coal thermal plants.

s: In which year did the Government of India pass the National Environment Tribunal Act?
x: The National Environment Tribunal Act was passed in 1995 (strict liability for hazardous-substance accidents) but never came into force; the NGT Act 2010 repealed it. 1997 is the NEAA Act.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: What is the main difference between Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
o: EIA focuses only on product design, while LCA focuses on project location
EIA and LCA both focus only on air pollution levels
EIA evaluates environmental impacts before a project starts, while LCA assesses impacts throughout the entire life of a product or process
EIA is used for agricultural projects only, while LCA is used for industrial projects only
x: EIA assesses the likely impacts of a specific project before it is implemented, while LCA follows a product or process from cradle to grave. Neither is limited to air pollution, design-stage location or one sector.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II

o: Legality of road construction in protected areas
Constitutionality of 2020 exemption from environmental clearance for road and pipeline projects
Compensation for displaced communities due to road projects
Regulation of heavy vehicle traffic on ecologically sensitive roads
x: Noble M. Paikada v. The Ministry of Science and Technology
x: The MoEFCC is India's nodal agency for UNEP (and for SACEP and ICIMOD) and for planning and implementing environmental and forestry programmes; the other ministries are not.

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
s:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Large Forest Fire Monitoring Programme launched in 2019?
Statement A: Forest Survey of India launched the beta version of the programme on 16-01-2019 using near real-time SNPP-VIIRS data.
Statement B: This programme is a part of the FAST 5.0 (FSI Fire Alerts System).
Statement C: FSI will track large fire events across the country and disseminate specific Large Fire alerts.
x: The Forest Survey of India launched the Large Forest Fire Monitoring Programme (beta, 16 Jan 2019) using near-real-time SNPP-VIIRS data to track large fires and send large-fire alerts. It is part of FAST 3.0 (Forest Fire Alert System), not 'FAST 5.0', so only B is incorrect.

x: The Botanical Survey of India (1890) is headquartered in Kolkata, West Bengal; Darjeeling, Bengaluru and Yercaud are not its HQ.

s:

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Which international event first introduced the concept of 'Sustainable Development' widely?

Printed key / many books: Stockholm 1972. Strictly: the term 'sustainable development' was popularised by the Brundtland Report (1987) and made a worldwide agenda at the Rio Earth Summit 1992 (Rocket Environment p.16, p.71).
Of the options, the Stockholm Conference of 1972 first put environment and development together on the world agenda, so it is the printed answer; Paris 2015 and Kyoto 1997 are climate treaties. The term itself came from the Brundtland Report (1987) and Rio 1992 spread it worldwide.

s:
